title: Instrument Panel Speaker
introduction:
For vehicles with the documented MyFord Touch interface, reaching the instrument panel speaker starts with the surrounding trim, then the grille. I treat this as opening fitted packaging: release each attachment before asking the next layer to move. The speaker wiring also has separate attachment points, so freeing the speaker means more than unplugging its electrical connector.

This guide covers removal and refitting, including the linked finish-panel access procedure and its optional ICM connection. It does not diagnose an audio complaint or establish that the speaker needs replacement.

requirements.category: Match the documented audio interface before starting

items.name: MyFord Touch interface required for this complete workflow
items.detail: Before dismantling anything, confirm that the fitted system has the documented MyFord Touch Home screen with the lower-left Entertainment corner, AM/FM tabs and the Power, VOL, TUNE and Seek controls described in the completion check. This workflow narrows the source’s SYNC 2/SYNC 3 heading to the interface supported by the supplied owner instructions. If the car has SYNC 3 or a different interface, stop before dismantling and obtain the complete matching owner control sequence and applicable repair instructions; this article does not verify that branch.

items.name: Trim removal and tightening
items.detail: Have an Interior Trim Remover for the RH instrument panel trim and center finish panel, plus a torque wrench suitable for the speaker mounting-bolt specification given in the removal instructions.

items.name: Read the applicable precautions
items.detail: Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting.

items.name: Remote start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye and ear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Sharp edges
items.detail: Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal instructions before beginning; they also contain information needed during installation.
edits.why: The speaker mounting-bolt tightening specification appears alongside removal, so keep it available for refitting.

edits.text:
Remove the instrument panel center finish panel. First, use an Interior Trim Remover to release the clips securing the narrow RH trim panel beside the outer edge of the glove compartment, then remove that trim panel. Next, use the trim remover to release the center finish panel clips across the fascia around the center vents and gauges and above the glove compartment. If the optional ICM is fitted, unplug its electrical connector at the rear of the finish panel before taking the panel away. Viewed from the rear of the panel, the connector withdraws from the ICM socket toward the right of that rear view.
Refer to: Instrument Panel Center Finish Panel (501-12 Instrument Panel and Console, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The RH trim comes off before the larger finish panel. I keep the optional rear connection in mind while freeing the fascia so the wiring does not become its last attachment. The linked procedure shows the panel with optional ICM; its rear-view connector direction is relative to that view. See [Instrument Panel Center Finish Panel](#/document/G1693976).

edits.text: Lift the instrument panel speaker grille upward from its exposed front edge, following the removal arrow, and remove it.
edits.why: Removing the grille exposes the speaker and its mounting flange. The blue area identifies the grille being removed.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts at opposite ends of the speaker flange. Detach the harness attachment beneath the rectangular component above the speaker and the separate attachment beside the upright harness run. Remove the instrument panel speaker, disconnecting its electrical connector as described below.
edits.why: The main drawing marks separate harness releases: a downward movement beneath the rectangular component and a leftward movement beside the upright harness run, relative to that drawing. These attachments are additional to the electrical plug shown in the speaker inset; unplugging alone does not free the harness.

edits.text:
Disconnect the electrical connector at the back of the speaker by withdrawing the plug from its socket, toward the right in the inset's rear view.
Speaker mounting-bolt installation torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: The inset identifies the speaker connection separately from the harness attachments. The tightening value applies to the speaker mounting bolts during installation.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order. Reconnect the plug at the back of the speaker and restore the harness attachments beneath the rectangular component and beside the upright harness run. Seat the speaker and install its mounting bolts, tightening them to the specification given above. Lower the speaker grille back into position and secure its attachments. If the optional ICM is fitted, insert its connector into the socket on the rear of the finish panel, reversing the unplugging movement toward the left in the rear view. Refit the center finish panel and engage its clips, then refit the RH trim panel and engage its clips.
edits.why:
Working back through the layers restores the wiring attachments as well as the visible trim. I account for both harness attachment points before covering the speaker; a tidy grille should not hide an unfinished connection.

After all wiring and trim are restored, keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and the engine stopped. With the valid key inside, start from ignition OFF and press the start button without pressing either pedal to switch the ignition ON without starting the engine. For the documented MyFord Touch interface, if the audio is OFF, press the audio Power button to turn it ON; if it has already resumed ON, leave it ON rather than toggling it. Touch the Home icon, then the lower-left Entertainment corner and the AM or FM tab. Turn TUNE or press Seek to find a familiar station, then turn VOL to a comfortable level and listen for sound from the replaced speaker. This is an ordinary function check, not fault isolation. After the check, press audio Power to turn the audio off, then press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. Remove the key. If the sound is absent or abnormal, keep that OFF/key-out state before reopening trim or checking a connector. The keyless controls and audio interface are described in the supplied Ford Mustang owner’s manual.
